hypotheses.statement: In advanced NSCLC receiving first-line systemic therapy, STK11 loss-of-function is associated with shorter overall survival to a similar degree in immune-checkpoint-inhibitor-containing regimens and in platinum-doublet regimens without an ICI, i.e. the treatment-by-STK11 interaction on overall survival is null and the marker is prognostic rather than predictive.

origin.rationale: This is the central declared direct contradiction in the graph (C-003 vs C-013) and the one the whole field turns on. The resistance claim rests almost entirely on single-arm, ICI-only cohorts (C-003, C-039, C-040) which cannot separate prognosis from prediction. Every design in the graph that carries a non-ICI control arm points the other way: Papillon-Cavanagh's interaction HR is 1.05 (p=0.785) for PFS and 1.13 (p=0.540) for OS (C-012, C-013); Shire reports HR 1.4 for STK11 on first-line chemotherapy with no ICI (C-037) and the same point estimate, nonsignificant, on first-line ICI (C-038); KEYNOTE-042 randomization shows a numerically LARGER pembrolizumab benefit in STK11-mutants (C-018). I expect the data to favour C-012/C-013/C-037 over C-003/C-039. The mapper found no verified post-2022 cohort with n>500 reporting a formal treatment-by-STK11 interaction test, and my own searches did not find one either; that exact design is the gap. A large clinicogenomic cohort with both ICI-treated and chemotherapy-only first-line patients is uniquely able to supply it.

prior_negative_evidence.summary: Looked directly and found nothing: no interaction between STK11 mutation and anti-PD-1/PD-L1 treatment on real-world PFS (HR 1.05, 0.76-1.44, p=0.785) or OS (HR 1.13, 0.76-1.67, p=0.540). This is the strongest existing null and it substantially discounts novelty; the remaining gap is that it is a 2020 non-squamous-only cohort with 574 ICI-treated patients, underpowered for subgroup interaction and predating chemo-immunotherapy as the dominant first-line standard.

prior_negative_evidence.identifier: J Clin Oncol 43 (16_suppl) e20504, ASCO 2025 abstract
prior_negative_evidence.summary: Meta-analysis of six randomized and one retrospective comparative study: chemo-immunotherapy retained an OS benefit over chemotherapy alone despite STK11 mutation (HR 0.80, 0.67-0.97), KEAP1 (0.76, 0.59-0.98) and KRAS (0.67, 0.55-0.82). A randomized-comparator null for the predictive interpretation. Conference abstract only, not a full paper.

Commentary/analysis explicitly titled 'STK11/LKB1 and KEAP1 mutations in non-small cell lung cancer: Prognostic rather than predictive?' — the prognostic interpretation is already in print, so the novelty here is the formal interaction estimate at modern scale, not the idea.

exposure.description: STK11 loss-of-function alteration in the sequenced tumour
exposure.genomic_criteria: STK11 nonsense, frameshift, splice-site, or homozygous deletion, or a missense variant annotated oncogenic/likely-oncogenic; excludes variants of unknown significance
exposure.treatment_criteria: first-line systemic therapy containing an anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 agent (with or without platinum doublet)

comparator.description: Two explicit contrasts crossed in one model: (a) STK11 wild-type patients receiving the same first-line ICI-containing regimen, and (b) STK11 loss-of-function patients receiving first-line platinum-doublet chemotherapy with no ICI. The estimand is the ratio of the STK11 effect across the two treatment strata.

population.description: Adults with advanced or metastatic NSCLC who received first-line systemic therapy and had tumour next-generation sequencing covering STK11
inclusion: stage IIIB-IV or recurrent disease at start of first-line therapy
tumour NGS panel covering STK11, KRAS, KEAP1, TP53
exclusion: activating EGFR mutation or ALK/ROS1 fusion

hypotheses.proposed_endpoint_concept: overall survival from start of first-line systemic therapy
proposed_covariates: age at start of first-line therapy
ECOG performance status at treatment start
KRAS, KEAP1, TP53 and SMARCA4 co-mutation status
year of treatment initiation (era effects in ICI availability)
time from advanced diagnosis to sequencing report, with left truncation at the sequencing date to remove immortal time between diagnosis and genomic ascertainment

plausibility.causal_story: LKB1 loss removes AMPK-dependent restraint on mTORC1 and on anabolic one-carbon flux, raising proliferative capacity, lineage plasticity and metastatic competence; co-selected KEAP1/NRF2 activation adds broad cytoprotection against oxidative and cytotoxic stress. The survival deficit is therefore generated by tumour growth biology and is realised on platinum doublet as much as on PD-(L)1 blockade. The immune-evasion arm (STING silencing C-029/C-030, immunoproteasome failure C-031) is real but on this account is a minor contributor to total hazard. The chain predicts a non-null STK11 main effect in BOTH strata and a null interaction; it is falsified if the STK11 hazard is materially larger in the ICI stratum. That contrast is the estimand, so the hypothesis tests the mechanism rather than restating the association.
mechanism_steps: STK11 loss-of-function abolishes LKB1 kinase activity and hence AMPK activation under energy stress.
Loss of AMPK restraint de-represses mTORC1 and anabolic serine/one-carbon flux, supporting growth under nutrient and oxidative stress.
The resulting phenotype raises the hazard of death independently of which systemic agent is given.
Co-selected KEAP1/NRF2 activation blunts platinum cytotoxicity and oxidative effector mechanisms alike — again treatment-independent.
LKB1-dependent immune defects exist but contribute too little ICI-specific harm to generate a detectable interaction.
Therefore STK11 HR > 1 on ICI, STK11 HR > 1 of similar size on chemotherapy, ratio of the two ≈ 1.
alternative_explanations: Non-differential exposure misclassification (mutation is a poor proxy for functional loss, C-034) dilutes the effect equally in both arms and hides a genuine ICI-specific difference.

Comparator contamination: most first-line chemotherapy-only patients receive an ICI at second line, so OS from first-line start mixes both treatment histories and biases the interaction toward the null.
The modern chemotherapy-only stratum is small and atypical, so the interaction is driven by that stratum's peculiarities rather than by STK11 biology.
confounding_risks: Indication bias is the dominant threat: first-line platinum doublet WITHOUT an ICI now usually signals a contraindication (autoimmune disease, transplant, chronic steroids, organ dysfunction, poor PS). Those patients differ prognostically in ways no recorded covariate captures, and the interaction term is exactly what indication bias corrupts.
Era effects: the chemotherapy-only stratum concentrates before 2016 and after 2018 for different reasons while supportive care and later-line options changed; calendar year is a proxy, not a fix.

Immortal time: STK11 is ascertained at sequencing, which postdates diagnosis and often first-line start; left truncation at the sequencing report date is required and the truncation interval may itself differ by regimen.
Smoking: correlated with STK11 mutation, mutational burden, comorbidity and regimen tolerance, and captured unreliably.

Panel ascertainment: STK11 callability varies by panel version and tissue adequacy, so 'wild-type' mixes true wild-type with never-tested, and that mixture tracks institution and era, which track treatment.
Scale dependence: the hazard ratio is non-collapsible, so equal biological effects with unequal baseline hazards can yield a spuriously non-null interaction. Fix the interaction scale in advance.

hypotheses.statement: In advanced non-squamous NSCLC treated with first-line ICI-containing therapy, KEAP1 loss-of-function rather than STK11 loss-of-function carries the survival signal: in a model containing both genes, the KEAP1 term remains associated with shorter overall survival while the STK11 term attenuates towards the null relative to its unadjusted estimate.

origin.rationale: The graph disagrees about which of the two co-occurring genes is doing the work. In the Japanese C-CAT cohort KEAP1 was significantly detrimental (HR 1.89, 1.18-3.03, p=0.008) while STK11 was not (C-024 vs C-023). De Giglio reports the opposite ordering, with STK11 surviving adjustment for KEAP1 (C-026). Papillon-Cavanagh finds neither interacts with treatment (C-012, C-014). The two genes co-occur often enough that most published STK11 estimates are partly KEAP1 estimates, and almost no cohort in the graph is large enough to hold one constant while estimating the other. I expect KEAP1 to dominate, because the NRF2-activated state it produces confers broad cytoprotection and chemo/radio-resistance that acts on survival through a treatment-independent route, whereas the STK11 signal in the graph repeatedly evaporates when a non-ICI arm or a KRAS-wildtype stratum is introduced. This is a mutual-adjustment question a large cohort answers well and a trial subgroup analysis answers badly.

prior_negative_evidence.summary: Prospective multicentre biomarker cohort in which NEITHER gene predicted primary resistance: STK11 OR 1.17 (0.634-2.17, p-adj 0.896), KEAP1 OR 0.663 (0.344-1.28, p-adj 0.58). A double null that weakens the premise that either gene carries a large ICI-specific signal. Preprint, not peer reviewed, second-line-plus population.

Already performed the mutual adjustment in the opposite direction and found STK11 detrimental to OS after adjusting for KRAS, TP53, KEAP1 and SMARCA4 (multivariable HR 1.97, p=0.025). Directly contradicts the direction I predict; recorded here so the prediction is scored against the strongest opposing prior result rather than a straw man. Single-centre, n=145.
No KEAP1-by-treatment interaction on rwPFS (HR 0.93, 0.67-1.28, p=0.653) or OS (HR 0.98, 0.66-1.45, p=0.913) — so if KEAP1 carries the signal it is also prognostic, not predictive.

exposure.description: KEAP1 loss-of-function alteration, estimated jointly with STK11 loss-of-function in the same model
exposure.genomic_criteria: KEAP1 nonsense, frameshift, splice-site, homozygous deletion, or oncogenic/likely-oncogenic missense; STK11 defined identically and entered as a separate term with a KEAP1 x STK11 product term

comparator.description: Patients wild-type for both KEAP1 and STK11 receiving the same first-line ICI-containing regimen; the single-mutant strata (KEAP1-only, STK11-only) are the two contrasts of interest against that common reference.

population.description: Adults with advanced non-squamous NSCLC on first-line ICI-containing therapy with panel sequencing covering both STK11 and KEAP1
inclusion: panel covers STK11 and KEAP1 with adequate coverage for both

hypotheses.proposed_endpoint_concept: overall survival from start of first-line ICI-containing therapy
proposed_covariates: sequencing panel identity and gene coverage (KEAP1 and STK11 callability differ across panels)
left truncation at sequencing report date

plausibility.causal_story: KEAP1 loss-of-function prevents CUL3-mediated degradation of NRF2, so NRF2 accumulates constitutively and drives a glutathione/thioredoxin/NQO1 antioxidant program with glutaminolysis dependence. That state resists platinum-induced and ROS-mediated killing and supports proliferation under stress, shortening survival on any cytotoxic backbone; constitutive NRF2 also dampens tumour-intrinsic cGAS-STING output, lowering T-cell recruitment. Because STK11 and KEAP1 co-occur far above chance, an STK11 coefficient fitted without a KEAP1 term absorbs part of the KEAP1 effect. Prediction: with both terms present KEAP1 survives and STK11 attenuates. The falsifiable step is the assignment of the shared signal to the NRF2 side — C-026 did this adjustment and found the opposite ordering.
mechanism_steps: KEAP1 loss-of-function blocks CUL3/KEAP1-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of NRF2.
Constitutive NRF2 induces a broad antioxidant and detoxification program plus glutaminolysis dependence.
That program lowers the killing efficiency of platinum and of oxidative effector mechanisms and supports growth under stress — no ICI required for the penalty to appear.
NRF2 activation additionally suppresses tumour-intrinsic type I interferon, lowering CXCL9/10 and T-cell recruitment (a smaller, immune component).
Because the genes co-occur, the marginal STK11 association is partly a KEAP1 association carried by co-occurrence.
In a joint model KEAP1 retains its coefficient and STK11 moves toward the null relative to its unadjusted value.
alternative_explanations: The reverse partition is true and STK11 carries the signal: C-026 reports multivariable HR 1.97 for STK11 after adjustment for KRAS, TP53, KEAP1 and SMARCA4 — an opposing result, not an absence of evidence.
Neither gene is causal: both mark a shared aggressive, low-immune transcriptional state, and the mutual-adjustment ordering is then decided by which gene the panel measures better, not by biology.

Attenuation of the STK11 term is produced by non-collapsibility of the Cox hazard ratio rather than by confounding — adding any strong prognostic covariate shifts other coefficients toward the null even when it is not a confounder, so part of the predicted pattern arises with zero causal contribution from KEAP1.
confounding_risks: Non-collapsibility, as above: because the hypothesis compares an adjusted with an unadjusted coefficient, some predicted attenuation is guaranteed by the model form. The informative content is which gene retains an association, not the size of the shift.
Collinearity: strong co-occurrence makes both coefficients unstable and the ordering fragile, and the identifying single-mutant strata are the smallest cells.

Ascertainment, missing-not-at-random: KEAP1 entered several commercial panels later than STK11, so co-mutation status is systematically missing for older assays and late-adopting institutions; that missingness tracks era and treatment.
Smoking: a common cause of KEAP1 mutation, STK11 mutation and worse outcome, recorded unreliably.

Prognostic vs predictive: ICI-only design, so whichever gene wins cannot be shown to be ICI-specific. C-014 reports no KEAP1-by-treatment interaction, so the prior expectation is that the winner is prognostic.
Immortal time via sequencing-conditioned entry; left truncation at the sequencing report date is required.

hypotheses.statement: The association between STK11 loss-of-function and shorter overall survival on immune checkpoint inhibition is smaller in patients of East Asian genetic ancestry than in patients of European genetic ancestry with advanced lung adenocarcinoma, i.e. genetic ancestry modifies the STK11 effect.

origin.rationale: The gap report classifies C-003 vs C-023 as a direct contradiction with no context difference recorded, but the cohorts differ on exactly one thing the mapper could not encode as context: ancestry. Skoulidis (US, ancestry unreported) finds OS HR 1.99; the Japanese C-CAT cohort of 343 finds no significant STK11 OS effect while KEAP1 remains significant in the same model. There is a mechanistic reason to expect a real difference rather than noise: STK11 truncating mutations are strongly tobacco-associated, and East Asian lung adenocarcinoma cohorts carry a far higher never-smoker fraction, so an East Asian STK11-mutant tumour is more often a low-smoking-signature tumour whose STK11 event sits in a different co-mutation background (fewer KRAS, more EGFR-adjacent biology). If the STK11 'effect' is partly a marker for smoking-driven aggressive biology, it should shrink where that background is absent. The mapper found no US cohort with ancestry annotation analysing STK11 x ICI at all; a clinicogenomic cohort with genetically inferred ancestry can test this directly instead of comparing across papers.

prior_negative_evidence.identifier: PMC8577674, 'Disparities in Tumor Mutational Burden, Immunotherapy Use, and Outcomes Based on Genomic Ancestry in NSCLC'
prior_negative_evidence.summary: Looked at ICI outcomes stratified by genomic ancestry and reported that the TMB-survival relationship held across ancestral groups; it did not report an STK11-by-ancestry interaction, so the specific gap survives, but it shows the ancestry-stratified outcome analysis is a route others have already walked without finding an STK11 signal worth reporting.

Ancestry-associated co-alteration landscape of KRAS/EGFR-altered non-squamous NSCLC: STK11 and KEAP1 co-alteration frequencies differ by ancestry (higher in European and African ancestry KRAS-mutant tumours), but the paper reports prevalence only and states the outcome implication as an expectation, not a result. No effect estimate exists to discount.

The Japanese null itself: in 343 lung adenocarcinoma patients on ICIs, KEAP1 and TP53 were associated with inferior OS and STK11 was not. This is a genuine buried-ish negative for STK11 in an East Asian population and it is the reason to predict attenuation rather than merely to note that nobody looked.

exposure.description: STK11 loss-of-function in patients of East Asian genetic ancestry
exposure.genomic_criteria: STK11 nonsense, frameshift, splice-site, homozygous deletion, or oncogenic/likely-oncogenic missense; genetic ancestry assigned from germline-informative markers on the sequencing panel where available, otherwise self-reported race/ethnicity as a fallback with the two analyses reported separately
exposure.treatment_criteria: any line of anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy, with line entered as a covariate

comparator.description: STK11 loss-of-function patients of European genetic ancestry receiving the same class of therapy, with STK11 wild-type patients of each ancestry group as the within-stratum reference; the estimand is the ratio of the two ancestry-specific STK11 hazard ratios.

population.description: Adults with advanced lung adenocarcinoma treated with ICI-containing therapy in a US clinicogenomic cohort with genetic ancestry annotation
inclusion: ancestry assignable from genomic or recorded demographic data
at least one ICI-containing line of therapy
exclusion: EGFR-activating mutation or ALK/ROS1 fusion, which would confound the never-smoker-enriched stratum

hypotheses.proposed_endpoint_concept: overall survival from start of the first ICI-containing line of therapy
proposed_covariates: smoking status and pack-years (the primary competing explanation for any ancestry difference)
left truncation at sequencing report date

plausibility.causal_story: As proposed: East Asian ancestry associates with a higher never-smoker fraction, so an STK11 event there more often sits in a low-tobacco-signature, KRAS-wildtype background; if the STK11 association is largely a marker for smoking-driven aggressive biology and KRAS-dependent STING silencing, it shrinks where that background is absent. The arithmetic is coherent but every causal node is smoking or co-mutation status — measured directly and adjusted. There is no ancestry-to-LKB1 step anywhere in the chain, so the mechanism makes no prediction that the covariates do not make better, and the ancestry label contributes only confounding.
mechanism_steps: East Asian genetic ancestry associates with a higher never-smoker fraction in lung adenocarcinoma. (Demographic, not mechanistic.)
Never-smoker tumours carry a lower tobacco mutational signature and fewer activating KRAS alleles. (Directly measured; a covariate.)

If the STK11 effect requires a KRAS-driven metabolic background (C-029/C-030) or is partly a smoking marker, it is smaller in that background. (This is the content of H-009 and H-004, not of ancestry.)
Therefore the STK11 hazard ratio is smaller in East Asian than European ancestry patients — which follows only if the ancestry term is left unadjusted for the very variables that generate it.
alternative_explanations: The entire ancestry difference is smoking and co-mutation composition, which is directly estimable and makes the ancestry contrast redundant.

Cross-cohort artefact: C-023 differs from the US positives in ICI access, line of therapy and panel content, and its abstract names KEAP1 and TP53 while simply omitting STK11 — a reporting difference, not an effect estimate.
Differential ascertainment: panels and variant-calling thresholds differ across institutions serving different ancestry populations, so the exposure is measured differently in the two strata.
confounding_risks: Ancestry in a US clinicogenomic cohort is confounded with treating institution, insurance, socioeconomic position, time from symptom onset to treatment, and access to later-line therapy — all strongly prognostic and none separable here.
Smoking is simultaneously the proposed mechanism, the leading confounder and an adjustment covariate: adjusting removes the hypothesis, not adjusting removes the interpretation.
Self-reported race as a fallback misclassifies admixed patients non-randomly and correlates with the institutional confounders above.

Excluding EGFR/ALK removes most of the never-smoker East Asian stratum; conditioning on ancestry-linked never-smoker enrichment AND absence of a canonical driver conditions on two descendants of a common cause, a collider-stratification risk.
Prognostic vs predictive: ICI-only, no comparator arm, so even a clean ancestry interaction could not distinguish modification of the treatment effect from modification of the disease course.
Immortal time via sequencing-conditioned entry, with truncation intervals differing by institution and hence by ancestry composition.
plausibility.reject_reason: The exposure is a proxy for variables already in the model. Every link in the chain after 'East Asian ancestry' is a smoking or co-mutation variable — higher never-smoker fraction, lower tobacco signature, fewer KRAS alleles — and smoking status, pack-years, KRAS and KEAP1 status are all entered as covariates in the same model. Adjusted, the ancestry term tests nothing new; unadjusted, this is a smoking analysis wearing an ancestry label. No step runs from germline ancestry to LKB1 signalling, STING regulation or antigen processing. The one route that could have made it mechanistic — germline HLA class I supertype diversity, which does vary by ancestry and would modify precisely the presentation step LKB1 loss degrades (C-031) — is neither proposed nor recoverable from the stated exposure definition. The empirical anchor is not an ancestry contrast: C-023 is a Japanese national-database cohort compared across papers with US cohorts differing in health system, ICI access, line distribution, referral pattern and panel content. Within a single US cohort the East-Asian-versus-European contrast is confounded with institution, insurance, socioeconomic position and time to treatment, none of which the design separates. Finally, the same never-smoker premise is used by H-004 to predict a LARGER STK11 effect and here to predict a SMALLER one, which shows the premise fixes no direction and cannot support either.

hypotheses.statement: Among never-smokers with advanced NSCLC receiving first-line ICI-containing therapy, STK11 loss-of-function is associated with a larger reduction in overall survival relative to STK11 wild-type than it is among ever-smokers, i.e. smoking status modifies the STK11 effect in the direction of a stronger effect in never-smokers.

origin.rationale: Smoking is unspecified in 48 of 50 claims and is the graph's first-order confounding gap. The reason to expect a genuine difference, rather than merely noting nobody looked, is a specificity argument: in heavy smokers STK11 mutation is one of many tobacco-signature truncating events and travels with a high-TMB, inflamed background that partly offsets it, so an STK11 call there is a weak proxy for functional LKB1 loss. In never-smokers an STK11 truncating event is far less likely to be incidental, and Deng et al. found the counterintuitive result that LKB1 deficiency correlates with ELEVATED TMB specifically in NSCLCs from non-smokers (C-032) while still compromising immunoproteasome-dependent antigen presentation (C-031) and STING-dependent priming (C-029). That is the cleanest possible setting for the mechanism: high neoantigen supply, broken presentation, no smoking-driven inflammation to mask it. If the mechanism is real the effect should be larger, not smaller, where the confounder is absent — which is the opposite of what a pure-confounding account predicts, so the two accounts are distinguishable.

prior_negative_evidence.identifier: PMID 34740862 (Ricciuti, JTO 2022) as reported in secondary summaries
prior_negative_evidence.summary: An ever-smoker subgroup was analysed and STK11 and KEAP1 had no impact on immunotherapy efficacy among KRAS-wildtype/EGFR-wildtype/ALK-wildtype tumours and among ever smokers. This is a partial null in the ever-smoker stratum. It does not close the never-smoker stratum, which was not reported, but it does mean the smoking dimension has been touched and the novelty is in the never-smoker arm specifically.

Real-world dose-dependent analysis of smoking status and cumulative smoking dose as a prognostic stratifier in advanced NSCLC immunotherapy. Establishes that smoking dose itself shifts ICI outcomes, which is the main confounding pathway this hypothesis must adjust for; it reports no STK11 interaction.

inclusion: smoking status recorded and classifiable as never versus ever

proposed_covariates: pack-years as a continuous term within ever-smokers
tumour mutational burden (on the causal path, so reported with and without adjustment)
misclassification of NLP-extracted smoking status as a sensitivity analysis

plausibility.causal_story: In an ever-smoker tumour, tobacco mutagenesis generates many truncating passenger events, so an STK11 truncating call has lower positive predictive value for complete functional LKB1 loss, and the accompanying high-neoantigen inflamed background partly offsets whatever defect exists. In a never-smoker tumour an STK11 event is much more likely a selected driver with a second hit, so misclassification is lower; LKB1 loss there still raises mutational burden (C-032, observed in non-smokers specifically) while STING silencing (C-029/C-030) and immunoproteasome failure (C-031) block conversion of that supply into a CD8 response, with no smoking-driven inflammation to compensate. Net: a larger STK11 hazard among never-smokers. This is a mechanism rather than subgroup fishing because the pure-confounding account predicts the effect should SHRINK where smoking is absent, so the sign of the interaction discriminates.
mechanism_steps: Tobacco mutagenesis produces a high background rate of truncating events, so among ever-smokers some STK11 truncating calls are passengers or subclonal and do not abolish LKB1 function.
The exposure is therefore more misclassified in ever-smokers, attenuating the estimate in that stratum.
In never-smokers an STK11 event is more likely clonal, biallelic and functionally complete, so the downstream chain is actually engaged.
LKB1 deficiency raises TMB in non-smokers specifically (C-032): neoantigen supply is present while presentation and priming are broken (C-031, C-029).
Ever-smoker tumours carry a smoking-driven inflamed microenvironment that partially substitutes for missing innate priming; never-smoker tumours do not.
Therefore the STK11 hazard ratio is larger among never-smokers — the opposite sign to the pure smoking-confounding account.
alternative_explanations: Chance in a small stratum: never-smoker, EGFR/ALK-wildtype, STK11-mutant NSCLC is a rare cell and an interaction estimated there is unstable.

Residual driver heterogeneity: after excluding EGFR and ALK the never-smoker stratum is enriched for MET exon 14, RET and ERBB2 biology with distinct prognosis and ICI sensitivity, so the interaction could be a driver-composition effect.
Non-random NLP misclassification of smoking status (light and remote histories recorded inconsistently) pushes genuinely exposed patients into the never-smoker cell.
confounding_risks: Collider stratification: conditioning on never-smoker status AND absence of EGFR/ALK conditions on two descendants of the same tumour-origin biology, which can induce association between STK11 and unmeasured prognostic factors within the stratum.
Smoking dose is the effect modifier and is measured worst at the never/ever boundary that defines the strata; pack-year capture is biased toward heavier smokers.

Prognostic vs predictive: no non-ICI arm, so a positive interaction could equally be a modified prognostic effect. The hypothesis is materially stronger if crossed with the chemotherapy stratum of H-001.
TMB lies on the causal path (C-032) yet is listed as a covariate; adjusted and unadjusted estimates answer different questions and must not be pooled.
Differential ascertainment: never-smokers are sequenced earlier and more completely because driver testing is standard in that group, so left-truncation intervals differ between the compared strata.
Indication: never-smokers with PD-L1-low disease receive chemo-immunotherapy more often than monotherapy, so regimen composition differs across interaction cells.

hypotheses.statement: In patients aged 75 or older with advanced NSCLC receiving first-line ICI-containing therapy, STK11 loss-of-function is associated with a larger reduction in overall survival relative to STK11 wild-type than in patients under 65.

origin.rationale: The mapper found no claim reporting an age-stratified STK11 effect and no cohort reporting an age range in a capturable form. The reason to expect an age difference is the myeloid arm of the mechanism: Koyama reports that LKB1 deficiency drives tumour-infiltrating neutrophil accumulation with T-cell-suppressive cytokine production (C-027), and that arm is contested rather than refuted (Skoulidis failed to reproduce it in a different mouse model, C-009). Ageing independently shifts haematopoiesis toward myeloid output and raises circulating neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio while shrinking the naive T-cell repertoire available for de novo priming. If the LKB1-loss phenotype works partly by adding myeloid suppression on top of a defective priming signal, its cost should be highest in hosts whose priming reserve is already lowest. This is also a subgroup that randomized trials systematically under-enrol and a real-world cohort over-represents, which is exactly the comparative advantage argument. A null here would be informative, because it would push the mechanism toward the tumour-intrinsic STING/antigen-presentation account (C-029, C-031) and away from the host-myeloid account.

prior_negative_evidence.summary: Age was included only as an adjustment covariate; no age-stratified STK11 estimate or age interaction was reported. Searches for an STK11-by-age interaction in NSCLC immunotherapy returned no primary result, so this gap is genuinely open rather than quietly filled — but it is also open because nobody has thought it interesting, which is the weaker kind of gap.

exclusion: patients aged 65-74, who are excluded from the primary contrast and reported separately

plausibility.causal_story: As proposed: LKB1 loss increases CXCL/IL-6-driven neutrophil and MDSC accumulation with T-cell suppression (C-027, mouse), and ageing independently skews haematopoiesis toward myeloid output while shrinking the naive T-cell repertoire, so the two insults compound and the STK11 penalty is largest after 75. The compounding step is asserted, not demonstrated; the underlying myeloid claim was not reproduced in a second mouse model (C-009); and the opposite saturation argument follows just as readily from the same biology. No step predicts ICI-specificity, and the age contrast is dominated by competing mortality and treatment-intensity differences.
mechanism_steps: LKB1 loss increases pro-inflammatory cytokine output and tumour-associated neutrophil/MDSC accumulation. (C-027, mouse; contradicted by C-009 in a different mouse model.)
Those myeloid cells suppress T-cell activity in the tumour microenvironment. (Mouse.)
Ageing shifts haematopoiesis toward myeloid output and shrinks the naive T-cell repertoire available for de novo priming. (Established, but host-level and not STK11-specific.)
The two effects compound rather than saturate, so the marginal cost of LKB1-driven suppression is larger in an aged host. (Asserted; the saturation alternative predicts the opposite sign.)
Therefore the STK11 hazard ratio is larger at 75+ than under 65. (Direction not fixed by the preceding steps.)
alternative_explanations: Competing non-cancer mortality in the 75+ stratum dilutes any tumour-genotype effect on overall survival, which predicts a smaller — not larger — STK11 hazard ratio in the elderly, so the leading alternative reverses the claimed direction.

Regimen composition: patients 75+ preferentially receive ICI monotherapy or dose-attenuated chemo-immunotherapy, so an apparent age-by-STK11 interaction may be a regimen-by-STK11 interaction (which is H-010's question) mislabelled as age.
Selection into sequencing: fitter elderly patients are preferentially sequenced, so the 75+ genomic cohort is a survivor-selected subgroup with atypical prognosis.
confounding_risks: ECOG performance status and comorbidity burden are strongly age-correlated, poorly recorded in real-world data, and act directly on the endpoint; residual confounding on this axis alone can generate or erase the interaction.
Indication bias: regimen choice, dose intensity and early discontinuation all differ systematically after 75 and are only partially recorded.
Competing risks: overall survival in the elderly mixes cancer and non-cancer death, so the estimand is not the same quantity in the two age bands.
Prognostic vs predictive: ICI-only design with no comparator arm; a positive result cannot be attributed to checkpoint blockade.
Immortal time: sequencing-conditioned entry selects harder in the elderly, where early death before sequencing is more common.
Ascertainment: older patients are sequenced on smaller or older panels more often, so STK11 callability differs across the compared bands.
plausibility.reject_reason: The load-bearing step is a single mouse claim that failed replication in another mouse model within the same graph: C-027 (LKB1 loss drives T-cell-suppressive neutrophil accumulation) is contradicted by C-009, in which the same enrichment was explicitly not observed. Building an age-modification hypothesis on the contested limb of a contested preclinical mechanism is exactly the kind of reach stage 3 exists to stop. Worse, the chain does not fix the claimed direction. 'Myeloid suppression costs most where priming reserve is lowest' is one reading; the equally available saturation reading — a host who already primes poorly loses little more when the tumour also fails to prime — predicts a SMALLER STK11 effect in the elderly. A mechanism that supports both signs predicts neither. Nothing in the chain is ICI-specific either: immunosenescence plus an aggressive genotype predicts worse survival on any therapy, and with no non-ICI arm the design cannot tell the two apart. Finally, any age-band difference in a survival hazard is dominated by competing non-cancer mortality, ECOG and comorbidity, and by preferential assignment of monotherapy or attenuated regimens after 75 — all of which act on overall survival regardless of STK11 and none of which the listed covariates resolve. The candidate's own rationale concedes the gap is open 'because nobody has thought it interesting', which is the weaker kind of gap.

hypotheses.statement: The association between STK11 loss-of-function and shorter survival on anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy is weaker when the ICI is given in the second line or later after platinum-based chemotherapy than when it is given in the first line.

origin.rationale: Line of therapy is thinly covered: only 3 of 50 claims are second-line-plus, and they disagree with the first-line literature. PIONeeR, a prospective second-line-plus biomarker cohort of 305 sequenced patients, found STK11 unassociated with primary resistance (OR 1.17, p-adj 0.896) and unassociated with PFS (C-046). CheckMate-057, also second-line, is the source of the most extreme resistance claim but rests on six KL patients (C-004). There are two reasons to expect a genuinely smaller effect later in the treatment course rather than sampling noise. First, depletion of susceptibles: if STK11 marks aggressive biology, the STK11-mutant patients who survive first-line therapy to reach a second line are a selected, less aggressive subset, so the prognostic component of the effect is partly spent. Second, prior platinum exposure delivers cytotoxic antigen release and DNA damage over months, which is the one input that could partially compensate for silenced STING-dependent innate priming (C-029, C-030) before the ICI is ever given. Both accounts predict attenuation; distinguishing them is a second-stage question, but the attenuation itself is testable and would reconcile PIONeeR with the first-line cohorts.

prior_negative_evidence.summary: The relevant null itself: in a prospective second-line-plus cohort, neither STK11 (OR 1.17, 0.634-2.17, p-adj 0.896) nor KEAP1 (OR 0.663, 0.344-1.28, p-adj 0.58) predicted primary resistance. Someone looked in this exact population and found nothing, so a hypothesis claiming a large second-line STK11 effect would be dead; the hypothesis proposed here is the attenuation itself, which the null supports rather than kills.

The one randomized second-line datapoint reports ORR 0% in 6 KL patients (p=0.047 across subgroups). Six patients cannot support or refute a line-of-therapy interaction, and citing it as evidence of second-line resistance is the error this hypothesis exists to correct.

best response and duration of the prior platinum line where recorded

plausibility.causal_story: As proposed: (a) patients who survive first-line therapy to receive a second-line ICI are selected against the aggressive STK11-driven phenotype, so the prognostic component is partly spent; (b) months of prior platinum deliver DNA damage and antigen release that partially substitute for silenced STING-dependent priming. Limb (b) is self-defeating, because the defect is in dsDNA sensing rather than in dsDNA supply — silencing STING removes the receptor, so more ligand changes nothing — and the parallel presentation defect (C-031) blocks the antigen-release route as well. Limb (a) is a description of survivorship bias. What remains is a prediction about a selected population, not about biology.
mechanism_steps: STK11-mutant patients with the most aggressive disease die or progress irrecoverably during first-line therapy. (Selection, not mechanism.)
Those reaching a second-line ICI are therefore a less aggressive subset, so the measured STK11 effect is smaller. (Restates the selection.)
Prior platinum generates DNA damage and cytosolic dsDNA. (True.)
That dsDNA restores innate priming in LKB1-deficient tumours. (FALSE on the graph's own mechanism: C-029 removes STING, the sensor for that ligand, so additional ligand cannot be sensed.)
Prior platinum releases tumour antigen that primes a CD8 response. (Undercut by C-031: the immunoproteasome and MHC-I presentation step is itself compromised.)
Therefore the STK11 effect is attenuated in later lines. (Follows from the selection limb only.)
alternative_explanations: Pure survivorship: the second-line cohort is conditioned on surviving first-line therapy, which removes the exposed patients with the largest hazard and mechanically shrinks the estimated effect.

PD-L1 composition: first-line monotherapy is restricted to TPS ≥50% while second-line monotherapy is not, so the two strata differ on the dominant effect modifier, and any line difference may be a PD-L1 difference.
Era and regimen drift: second-line monotherapy was standard in 2015-2018 and rare thereafter, so line of therapy proxies calendar time, supportive care and access to subsequent options.
confounding_risks: Immortal-time bias is at its maximum here: entry into the second-line stratum requires surviving the first line and being sequenced, and time-to-index-line adjustment does not repair conditioning on survival.
Structural PD-L1 imbalance between the strata being compared, as above.
Indication bias: who receives second-line monotherapy versus best supportive care after platinum failure depends on performance status and clinician judgement, not randomisation.
Prior-line response is a post-treatment variable on the causal path; adjusting for it induces collider bias, and not adjusting leaves the strata non-exchangeable.
Prognostic vs predictive: no non-ICI comparator in either stratum, so even a clean line interaction would not identify an ICI-specific effect.
Ascertainment: sequencing frequently postdates the first line, so second-line patients are systematically better ascertained than first-line ones.
plausibility.reject_reason: Neither limb of the proposed mechanism survives inspection. The platinum-compensation limb requires prior chemotherapy to restore innate priming by generating DNA damage and cytosolic dsDNA — but the LKB1 mechanism in this graph is loss of STING and hence loss of the capacity to SENSE cytosolic dsDNA (C-029/C-030), compounded by a compromised immunoproteasome (C-031). Followed honestly, the mechanism predicts that platinum cannot compensate in exactly the tumours where the sensor is silenced, so it does not support the claimed attenuation. The remaining limb, depletion of susceptibles, is not biology at all: it is survivorship selection, and a hypothesis whose prediction is 'the association is smaller in a group defined by having already survived' restates the selection process rather than proposing a mechanism. The comparison is additionally confounded by construction: first-line ICI monotherapy requires PD-L1 TPS ≥50% whereas second-line monotherapy is given irrespective of PD-L1, so the two strata differ systematically on the strongest known effect modifier in this literature, as well as on calendar era, prior-treatment response and performance status at the index line. Named confounders fully account for the predicted pattern.

hypotheses.statement: In advanced lung adenocarcinoma treated with anti-PD-1/PD-L1 monotherapy, the KRAS-mutant/STK11-mutant (KL) genotype is associated with a lower probability of durable clinical benefit than the KRAS-mutant/TP53-mutant (KP) genotype, and this ordering persists within each PD-L1 expression band.

origin.rationale: The KL/KP/K-only trichotomy is the single most cited result in this literature and it rests on a 2018 cohort of 174 patients, with six to seven patients per cell in the randomized CheckMate-057 component (C-001, C-004). Nine claims in the graph are flagged temporally stale and all nine come from that paper. What modern scale buys is specific and not merely more precision: enough KL patients to estimate the contrast WITHIN PD-L1 bands rather than across them. That matters because the original paper's own data show KL tumours are PD-L1-low (13.6% positive, 0% high, C-006) and STK11 mutation is roughly twice as frequent in PD-L1-negative tumours (C-050), so the headline KL-versus-KP response gap and the PD-L1 distribution are confounded by construction. Skoulidis argued the effect is partly PD-L1-independent on the basis of an ORR comparison with an unreported denominator (C-005). A cohort with thousands of ICI-treated adenocarcinomas and recorded PD-L1 can settle whether the genotype ordering survives PD-L1 stratification; if it does not, the KL category is largely a PD-L1 surrogate.

prior_negative_evidence.summary: Looked at pembrolizumab efficacy in the PD-L1-high stratum specifically and reported lower ORR with low STK11/LKB1 expression among TPS>=50% tumours (22% versus 41%), i.e. a positive result within the PD-L1-high band that partly pre-empts this hypothesis. Small single-institution study using expression rather than mutation, so the mutation-defined, adequately powered version remains open.

prior_negative_evidence.identifier: PMID 36709038 (KEYNOTE-042 exploratory analysis, Mok, Ann Oncol 2023)
prior_negative_evidence.summary: In a randomized PD-L1-positive population, pembrolizumab OS benefit versus chemotherapy was retained in STK11-mutants (HR 0.37, 0.16-0.86) and numerically exceeded the wild-type benefit (0.83, 0.65-1.05). A randomized result pointing away from PD-L1-independent STK11 resistance, in only 33 STK11-mutant patients.

PD-L1 TPS recorded

proposed_covariates: PD-L1 TPS band as the stratifying variable
specific KRAS codon/allele, since G12C and G12D differ in co-mutation background

plausibility.causal_story: LKB1 loss raises S-adenosylmethionine and hyperactivates DNMT1/EZH2, silencing STING (C-029/C-030); loss of cytosolic dsDNA sensing removes type I interferon output, lowering CXCL9/10 and CD8 recruitment (C-007) and lowering interferon-inducible PD-L1 (C-006, C-050). In parallel, compromised immunoproteasome activity and raised autophagic flux reduce MHC-I peptide supply (C-031). TP53 loss instead raises mutational burden and preserves an inflamed phenotype. Prediction: KL < K-only < KP for durable benefit, and — because presentation and priming defects are not reducible to surface PD-L1 — the ordering persists within PD-L1 bands. The falsifiable step is the last one: if PD-L1 level is a sufficient readout of the intact interferon axis, the ordering collapses within bands and KL is a PD-L1 surrogate.
mechanism_steps: LKB1 loss elevates SAM and hyperactivates DNMT1/EZH2 (C-030, cell line).
STING is epigenetically silenced, abolishing cytosolic dsDNA sensing (C-029).
Type I interferon output falls, reducing CXCL9/CXCL10 and hence CD8 recruitment (C-007, human ex vivo).
Independently, immunoproteasome activity falls and autophagic flux rises, reducing MHC-I peptide supply (C-031).
PD-1 blockade releases a brake on a response that, in KL tumours, was never primed or presented; KP tumours retain both steps.
Because the defects are upstream of and additional to surface PD-L1, the KL-versus-KP ordering persists within PD-L1 bands rather than collapsing.
alternative_explanations: KL is a PD-L1 surrogate: the ordering is generated entirely by the PD-L1 distribution (C-006: 13.6% positive, 0% high) and disappears once bands are held constant.
KL is prognostically worse on any therapy: the comparison has no non-ICI arm, and KL and KP differ in baseline growth kinetics as well as immunogenicity.

The comparator is itself an exposure: TP53 mutation raises TMB and alters chemosensitivity, so KL-versus-KP is a contrast of two active genotypes, and any ordering could be driven by KP's advantages rather than KL's defects.
confounding_risks: Stratifying on PD-L1 conditions on a downstream consequence of the exposure (STK11 loss lowers PD-L1), so the within-band estimate is a controlled direct effect and is open to collider bias from any unmeasured factor that raises both PD-L1 and survival.
Prognostic vs predictive: single-arm ICI design cannot distinguish an ICI-specific KL deficit from a general one; the same stratification on a chemotherapy arm would be needed.
Landmark/durable-benefit endpoints condition on surviving to the landmark, which favours the less aggressive genotype independently of treatment effect.
PD-L1 assay and clone heterogeneity, plus drift between archival specimen and treatment start, mis-sort patients between bands non-randomly.
KRAS allele composition (G12C vs G12D vs others) differs between KL and KP and carries its own smoking and co-mutation background.
Immortal time and panel ascertainment, as elsewhere: STK11 and TP53 callability differ by panel version and era.

hypotheses.statement: Among patients with PD-L1 TPS of at least 50% receiving first-line anti-PD-1 monotherapy, STK11 loss-of-function is not associated with shorter overall survival relative to STK11 wild-type, i.e. the apparent STK11 penalty in unstratified ICI cohorts is largely accounted for by the PD-L1-low distribution of STK11-mutant tumours.

origin.rationale: Skoulidis's PD-L1-conditioned claim (C-005) is the load-bearing argument that STK11 resistance is not merely a PD-L1 story, and it is a 2018 ORR comparison with an unreported denominator — the weakest evidence in the graph carrying the most weight. Everything else in the graph pushes the other way: KL tumours are PD-L1-low (C-006), STK11 mutation is enriched roughly two-fold in PD-L1-negative tumours (C-050), the pooled PD-L1 positivity estimate for STK11-mutants is 41.1% against 55.0% for wild-type (C-041), and in the randomized PD-L1-positive KEYNOTE-042 population STK11-mutants retained full pembrolizumab benefit (C-018). What modern scale buys is a PD-L1-high stratum with enough STK11-mutant patients to estimate a survival hazard rather than compare two response proportions — a stratum that has never existed at adequate size, since KEYNOTE-042 had 33 STK11-mutant patients across all PD-L1 bands. This hypothesis is directional and falsifiable in the clinically actionable direction: if it holds, PD-L1-high STK11-mutant patients should not be steered away from monotherapy.

prior_negative_evidence.summary: Reported the opposite result in the same stratum: ORR 22% versus 41% for low STK11/LKB1 expression among TPS>=50% NSCLC. Directly opposes the direction predicted here. Small, single-institution, expression-based rather than mutation-based, and response rather than survival, but it is the most on-point contrary evidence and it must count against novelty.

prior_negative_evidence.identifier: ILCN/WCLC reporting of the KEYNOTE-042 STK11/KEAP1 analysis
prior_negative_evidence.summary: Concluded that single-agent pembrolizumab is active against STK11- and KEAP1-mutated NSCLC and that monotherapy should remain a standard first-line option for PD-L1-positive disease regardless of STK11 or KEAP1 status. The conclusion this hypothesis predicts is therefore already asserted in a randomized setting; the novelty is confirming it at a scale that can support a PD-L1-high-restricted survival estimate.

plausibility.causal_story: Tumour PD-L1 (CD274) transcription in NSCLC is largely interferon-driven through JAK/STAT1, and the same interferon axis is what LKB1 loss disables via STING silencing (C-029/C-030) and what supplies CXCL9/10 for T-cell recruitment. A tumour carrying an STK11 mutation that nonetheless expresses PD-L1 at TPS ≥50% therefore has, by that chain, a functionally intact interferon response — because the variant does not abolish kinase activity, because the second allele is retained, or because a compensating route keeps the axis on. In such tumours the substrate that PD-1 blockade acts on (a pre-existing, interferon-driven, PD-L1-marked T-cell response under checkpoint restraint) is present, so the mutation should not mark resistance; in the PD-L1-low bands it should. The chain predicts both the direction (null in the high band) and the specificity (a gradient across bands, with PD-L1 superseding genotype), and it is falsified by a clear STK11 penalty at TPS ≥50%.
mechanism_steps: STING silencing after LKB1 loss removes tumour-intrinsic type I interferon output (C-029/C-030).
Interferon signalling through JAK/STAT1 is the principal inducer of tumour CD274 expression and of CXCL9/CXCL10.
Hence STK11-mutant tumours are systematically PD-L1-low and T-cell-poor (C-006, C-041, C-050, C-007) — PD-L1 is a functional readout of the axis, not an independent marker.

An STK11-mutant tumour with TPS ≥50% is therefore one in which the axis is intact, i.e. the mutation has not produced the functional deficiency (consistent with C-034, phenotype rather than mutation).
In that group PD-1 blockade has the substrate it needs, so survival should not differ from STK11 wild-type.
In the PD-L1-low bands the deficiency is present, so the penalty should appear — a gradient across bands, not a uniform effect.
alternative_explanations: The PD-L1-high stratum is smaller, so a null is a wide interval rather than an absence of effect; the claim requires an equivalence-style reading of the estimate, not just p > 0.05.
PD-L1-high STK11-mutant tumours differ on other grounds — histology, specimen site, prior radiation, time from biopsy — that independently predict better survival.
The contrary direct evidence: In Vivo 2020 reports lower ORR with low STK11/LKB1 expression specifically among TPS ≥50% tumours, which is the same stratum and the opposite direction.
confounding_risks: Conditioning on PD-L1 conditions on a downstream consequence of the exposure, so within-band comparison can induce collider bias if an unmeasured factor raises both PD-L1 and survival; the estimate is a controlled direct effect and should be labelled as one.
Assay heterogeneity: clone, platform and archival drift move patients across the 50% threshold non-randomly, and misallocation is likely differential by institution and era.
Indication bias: first-line monotherapy at TPS ≥50% is preferentially given to older, frailer or lower-burden patients, while fitter patients with bulky disease receive chemo-immunotherapy.
Prognostic vs predictive: without a chemotherapy comparator in the same stratum, a null is consistent both with 'no predictive effect' and with a prognostic effect offset by something else.
Immortal time via sequencing-conditioned entry, plus the requirement that a PD-L1 result predates treatment, which selects on workup completeness.
Panel ascertainment: STK11 callability and variant-classification thresholds differ across assays, and the null is exactly the result that exposure misclassification would manufacture.

hypotheses.statement: The association between STK11 loss-of-function and shorter overall survival on ICI-containing therapy is present in KRAS-mutant lung adenocarcinoma and absent in KRAS-wildtype lung adenocarcinoma, i.e. there is a KRAS-by-STK11 interaction on survival.

origin.rationale: The mechanism is the point, and it is specific rather than a co-occurrence observation. Kitajima showed that LKB1 loss silences STING through DNMT1 and EZH2 hyperactivation driven by elevated S-adenosylmethionine (C-029, C-030), and did so in a KRAS-driven context: the one-carbon and serine-glycine flux that raises SAM is downstream of oncogenic KRAS-driven anabolic metabolism. On that account LKB1 loss without an activating KRAS allele does not generate the methyl-donor surplus needed to hyperactivate the methyltransferases, so STING is retained and the tumour is not rendered innately blind. That predicts a conditional, not an additive, effect. The clinical shape already matches: Ricciuti reports STK11 and KEAP1 worsen ICI outcomes among KRAS-mutant but not KRAS-wildtype LUAD (C-015 versus C-016) and that the distinct immunophenotype appears only in KRAS-mutant tumours (C-017), and the gap report classifies this pair as an effect modifier rather than a contradiction. What is missing is a formal interaction term estimated with enough KRAS-wildtype STK11-mutant patients to distinguish a true null from an underpowered subgroup — that stratum is small in every published cohort and large in a modern clinicogenomic one.

prior_negative_evidence.summary: Reported the stratified result this hypothesis formalises, concluding that STK11 and KEAP1 confer worse outcomes among KRAS-mutant but not KRAS-wildtype LUAD. The stratified finding is therefore published; what is not published is a formal interaction test with a confidence interval on the interaction term, which is what distinguishes a real effect modification from two subgroups of different size.

Examined STK11/KEAP1/SMARCA4 co-mutations in RAS-activated but KRAS-wildtype metastatic NSCLC on ICIs and reported that the adverse association seen in KRAS-mutant disease was not clearly observed in the KRAS-wildtype population. A second, independent null in the KRAS-wildtype stratum, consistent with the predicted interaction but reducing the novelty of the stratified claim.

Did not stratify by KRAS and found no STK11-by-treatment interaction overall; if the KRAS-by-STK11 interaction is real, pooling across KRAS strata is one explanation for that null, which makes the two results compatible rather than contradictory.

The comparison of interest is the difference between the STK11 effect inside and outside the KRAS-mutant stratum.

plausibility.causal_story: Oncogenic KRAS drives glycolytic, glutaminolytic and serine-glycine one-carbon flux, which raises the S-adenosylmethionine pool. In the absence of LKB1/AMPK restraint that surplus hyperactivates DNMT1 and EZH2 (C-030), which methylate and silence STING (C-029), removing cytosolic dsDNA sensing and type I interferon output, reducing CXCL9/10 and CD8 recruitment (C-007) and leaving PD-1 blockade with little to release. Without an activating KRAS allele the methyl-donor surplus is not generated, the methyltransferases are not hyperactivated, STING is retained, and LKB1 loss does not render the tumour innately blind. The effect of STK11 loss is therefore conditional on KRAS rather than additive, and the product term — not two subgroup estimates — is the estimand. The falsifiable step is the KRAS-dependence of the SAM surplus: if LKB1 loss raises SAM in KRAS-wildtype tumours too, the interaction is null.
mechanism_steps: Oncogenic KRAS increases serine-glycine and one-carbon flux, raising the intracellular SAM pool.
LKB1 loss removes AMPK-dependent restraint on that anabolic program, so SAM accumulates further.
Elevated SAM hyperactivates DNMT1 and EZH2 (C-030, cell line).
DNMT1/EZH2 activity silences STING, abolishing cytosolic dsDNA sensing (C-029).
Type I interferon output falls, lowering CXCL9/CXCL10 and CD8 infiltration (C-007, human ex vivo; C-017, KRAS-mutant-only immunophenotype).
In KRAS-wildtype tumours steps 1-3 do not occur, STING is retained, and STK11 loss carries no comparable immune penalty — a positive KRAS x STK11 interaction on survival.
alternative_explanations: The KRAS-wildtype stratum is a mixture of MET exon 14, BRAF, RET and ERBB2-driven and never-smoker biologies with their own prognosis and ICI sensitivity, so an apparent interaction may be driver composition rather than KRAS-dependence.
Differential exposure quality: STK11 events in KRAS-wildtype tumours may less often be biallelic or clonal, so the interaction could be H-014's zygosity effect appearing in KRAS clothing.
The published 'absent in KRAS-wildtype' result is a nonsignificance claim in the smaller stratum; the interaction may be an artefact of unequal precision rather than unequal effect.
confounding_risks: Smoking: KRAS-mutant LUAD is heavily smoking-enriched and KRAS-wildtype LUAD is not, so stratifying on KRAS is partly stratifying on smoking, with all its prognostic baggage.
Prognostic vs predictive: no non-ICI arm, so a real KRAS-by-STK11 interaction may exist on chemotherapy too (C-037 shows a large STK11 effect with no ICI present) and would not be ICI-specific.
PD-L1 distribution differs between KRAS-mutant and KRAS-wildtype disease, and PD-L1 is partly downstream of the same interferon axis, so adjusting for it is adjusting for a mediator.
KEAP1 co-mutation frequency differs by KRAS status, so the interaction can be carried by KEAP1 unless modelled jointly (see H-002).
Panel ascertainment: KRAS hotspot coverage is near-universal while STK11 coverage is not, so the four genotype cells are not equally well measured.
Immortal time via sequencing-conditioned entry, plus the exclusion of EGFR/ALK, which reshapes the KRAS-wildtype reference cell.

hypotheses.statement: Among STK11-loss-of-function advanced non-squamous NSCLC patients, first-line platinum-doublet plus anti-PD-1 is associated with longer overall survival than first-line anti-PD-1 monotherapy, and the advantage of adding chemotherapy is larger in STK11-mutant than in STK11-wildtype patients.

origin.rationale: The graph's treatment coverage is lopsided — 22 claims on ICI monotherapy against 9 on chemo-immunotherapy — and the head-to-head question clinicians actually face has never been asked of either arm. The mechanism gives a directional prediction rather than a hedge. LKB1 loss silences STING-dependent innate priming (C-029, C-030) and compromises immunoproteasome-dependent antigen presentation (C-031); both are the steps by which PD-1 blockade alone converts a pre-existing T-cell response into tumour control. When those steps are broken, a checkpoint antibody has little to release, which fits the PD-L1-low, T-cell-poor phenotype (C-006, C-041, C-050). Platinum chemotherapy does not depend on either step for its direct cytotoxic effect. So the expected pattern is that STK11-mutant patients lose relatively more by having chemotherapy withheld than wild-type patients do. Notably this is the opposite framing from the trial literature, which asks whether adding the ICI to chemotherapy still helps; that question already has a randomized answer, and this one does not, because no trial randomizes monotherapy against chemo-immunotherapy within an STK11 stratum. It is precisely a real-world treatment-selection contrast.

prior_negative_evidence.identifier: J Clin Oncol 43 (16_suppl) e20504, ASCO 2025 abstract
prior_negative_evidence.summary: Meta-analysis of six randomized and one comparative study (1596 patients) found chemo-immunotherapy retained OS benefit over chemotherapy alone despite STK11 (HR 0.80, 0.67-0.97), KEAP1 (0.76) and KRAS (0.67) mutation. This closes the adjacent question — whether adding an ICI to chemotherapy still works in STK11-mutants — and any hypothesis phrased that way should not be proposed. It does not touch the monotherapy-versus-chemo-immunotherapy contrast proposed here.

In the 54 STK11-mutant patients, adding pembrolizumab to chemotherapy gave PFS HR 0.81 (0.44-1.47) and OS HR 0.75 (0.37-1.50) — both nonsignificant, against PFS HR 0.38 in wild-type. An underpowered subgroup that is routinely read as evidence of resistance; it constrains the size of any incremental-ICI effect but says nothing about withholding chemotherapy.

Reports that STK11/KEAP1-altered NSCLC is relatively resistant to standard PD-(L)1-plus-chemotherapy combinations and that adding CTLA-4 blockade abrogates that resistance. This weakens the present hypothesis materially: if chemo-immunotherapy is itself compromised in STK11-mutants, the predicted advantage over monotherapy may be small. Recorded because it cuts against the candidate.

plausibility.causal_story: PD-1 blockade works by removing a brake on an existing, primed, MHC-I-restricted CD8 response. Both the innate licence for that priming (STING/type I interferon, C-029/C-030) and the peptide supply that feeds it (immunoproteasome, C-031) are degraded by LKB1 loss, which is why STK11-mutant tumours are PD-L1-low and T-cell-poor (C-006, C-041, C-050). Platinum's direct cytotoxic effect — DNA adducts, replication-fork collapse, apoptosis — does not require either step. Withholding chemotherapy therefore removes the one reliably active modality in an STK11-mutant tumour while leaving an antibody with little to release, whereas in a wild-type tumour monotherapy still has a working immune substrate. Prediction: the survival advantage of chemo-immunotherapy over monotherapy is larger in STK11-mutants, i.e. a positive regimen-by-STK11 interaction.
mechanism_steps: LKB1 loss silences STING and removes type I interferon-dependent licensing of priming (C-029/C-030).
LKB1 loss compromises immunoproteasome activity and raises autophagic flux, reducing MHC-I peptide supply (C-031).
PD-1 blockade alone therefore has little pre-existing response to release in STK11-mutant tumours, consistent with their PD-L1-low, T-cell-poor phenotype.
Platinum kills tumour cells by direct DNA damage, a route that does not require STING sensing or immunoproteasome function.
Hence the incremental value of the chemotherapy component is greater in STK11-mutant than in STK11-wildtype tumours.
Prediction: regimen-by-STK11 interaction favouring chemo-immunotherapy in the mutant stratum, estimated within a PD-L1 band where both regimens are genuinely used.
alternative_explanations: Genotype-aware prescribing: as STK11/KEAP1 status became routinely reported, clinicians began preferring chemo-immunotherapy for STK11-mutants, so the interaction can be manufactured by treatment selection that is itself a function of the exposure.

Platinum's contribution in combination is partly immunogenic cell death, which depends on the same sensing and presentation machinery — so the premise that the chemotherapy limb is LKB1-independent may be false, and the true interaction smaller or absent (consistent with Skoulidis 2024).

KEAP1/NRF2 co-mutation confers platinum resistance, so in the co-mutated subset the chemotherapy limb is blunted too and the interaction is diluted by co-mutation composition rather than by STK11 biology.
confounding_risks: Confounding by indication is the central threat and it is not removed by restricting to TPS ≥50%: within that band, chemo-immunotherapy is chosen for bulky, symptomatic, rapidly progressing disease while monotherapy is chosen for frail or lower-burden patients. These push the comparison in opposite directions and neither is well captured.

Exposure-dependent treatment assignment: if genotype is known before regimen choice, selection is a function of STK11 itself, which is precisely the route to a spurious interaction. Sequencing turnaround relative to treatment start must be modelled, not assumed.
Calendar trend: the strength of genotype-aware prescribing rises by year, so a year-by-regimen-by-genotype structure lurks behind any interaction estimate.
ECOG is recorded coarsely and inconsistently in real-world data yet is the dominant determinant of regimen intensity.
Prognostic vs predictive: both arms contain an ICI, so this compares two active regimens; it cannot establish that the STK11 effect is immune-mediated rather than a chemosensitivity effect.
Immortal time: patients must survive to receive and be sequenced for the index regimen, and the truncation interval differs between regimen groups.

hypotheses.statement: In advanced NSCLC treated with anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy, the survival advantage normally associated with high tumour mutational burden is attenuated or absent in STK11-loss-of-function tumours relative to STK11-wildtype tumours, i.e. STK11 status modifies the TMB-benefit relationship.

origin.rationale: This is the biomarker paradox the graph states but never tests. STK11 mutation is significantly associated with HIGH TMB (C-025, and C-032 in non-smokers specifically), yet with low PD-L1 (C-041) and low CD3+/CD8+ infiltration (C-007). The mechanism that reconciles them is explicit in the graph and is what makes this an interaction rather than a curiosity: TMB is a proxy for neoantigen supply, but supply only converts into a T-cell response if the peptides are processed and presented, and LKB1 loss compromises immunoproteasome activity and raises autophagic flux, degrading exactly that step (C-031), while STING silencing removes the innate signal that would license priming (C-029). So the causal chain from TMB to benefit is cut in the middle in STK11-mutant tumours. The clinical implication is concrete and untested at scale: TMB-high should not be used to justify ICI monotherapy in an STK11-mutant tumour. A cohort with paired TMB and STK11 calls on thousands of ICI-treated patients is the only design that can estimate this interaction.

prior_negative_evidence.summary: Reported that concurrent STK11 and KEAP1 mutation is associated with resistance to PD-(L)1 blockade despite high TMB. plausibility.causal_story: TMB is a proxy for neoantigen supply, and supply converts into clinical benefit only through a chain: proteasomal processing, MHC-I loading, surface presentation, recognition by a primed CD8 repertoire, then release of the checkpoint brake. LKB1 loss degrades the processing step (reduced immunoproteasome activity, increased autophagic flux, C-031) and removes the innate licence for priming (STING silencing, C-029), so additional neoantigens do not convert into additional recognition. That is why STK11-mutant tumours are simultaneously TMB-high (C-025, C-032), PD-L1-low (C-041) and T-cell-poor (C-007). Prediction: the slope of survival benefit on TMB is flatter, or flat, within the STK11-mutant stratum. The chain also predicts specificity — TMB carries little prognostic information off checkpoint blockade — so the interaction should be ICI-specific. The falsifiable step is that presentation, rather than supply, is rate-limiting.
mechanism_steps: Higher TMB yields more candidate neoantigenic peptides.
Those peptides require immunoproteasome processing and MHC-I loading to reach the cell surface; LKB1 loss compromises exactly this step (C-031).
Priming of a naive repertoire additionally requires innate licensing through STING-dependent type I interferon, which LKB1 loss silences (C-029/C-030).
With both steps degraded, marginal neoantigen supply produces no marginal T-cell recognition in STK11-mutant tumours.
PD-1 blockade can therefore release nothing extra despite a high TMB, consistent with the observed TMB-high/PD-L1-low/T-cell-poor triad.
Prediction: a negative TMB x STK11 interaction on survival under ICI, and no comparable interaction on chemotherapy.
alternative_explanations: Smoking is a common cause of both high TMB and STK11 mutation, and the TMB-survival relationship itself differs by smoking intensity, so the interaction may be a smoking-by-TMB effect relabelled.

Measurement error: panel-derived TMB is a noisy proxy for neoantigen supply, and error in an effect modifier attenuates interaction estimates non-uniformly across strata with different TMB distributions.

Ceiling effects: the TMB-benefit relationship flattens at the top of the range in any group, and STK11-mutant tumours sit higher in that range (C-025), so an apparent slope difference may be curvature rather than modification.
confounding_risks: Panel heterogeneity: TMB is not comparable across assays, panel choice tracks institution and era, and STK11 callability varies with the same panels — so both the exposure and the modifier are measured differently across the cohort.
Smoking, as above, with pack-year data poorly captured.

Prognostic vs predictive: with no non-ICI arm, an attenuated TMB slope in STK11-mutants cannot be shown to be ICI-specific, which is the entire clinical claim (do not use TMB-high to justify monotherapy).
Correlated exposure and modifier: STK11 mutation itself raises TMB, so the STK11-mutant/TMB-low cell is sparse and the interaction rests on the least populated corner.
KEAP1 collinearity: KEAP1 also raises TMB and shortens survival, so the interaction may be carried by KEAP1 unless modelled jointly.
Immortal time via sequencing-conditioned entry; and TMB is only available for patients with adequate tissue, which correlates with disease burden and biopsy site.

hypotheses.statement: In a first-line advanced NSCLC population analysed with a time-to-event rather than a binary endpoint, STK11 loss-of-function is associated with a modestly shorter time to progression or death on anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy, an association the PIONeeR primary-resistance analysis was structurally unable to detect.

origin.rationale: PIONeeR is the most rigorous negative in the graph: a prospective multicentre biomarker cohort in which STK11 was neither associated with primary resistance (OR 1.17, 0.634-2.17, p-adj 0.896) nor with PFS (C-046). It deserves to be taken seriously, and it is also the kind of null worth re-testing with a named fix rather than dismissing. Three specific features limit it. First, the primary endpoint is a binary primary-resistance label, and dichotomising a time-to-event outcome discards most of the information — with 58 STK11-mutant patients, an odds ratio of 1.17 is compatible with a hazard ratio in the 1.2-1.4 range that the pooled literature reports (C-039, HR 1.45). Second, the population is second-line-plus, where survivorship has already selected against the aggressive phenotype (this is the same effect H-006 tests directly). Third, p-values are adjusted across a large multimodal biomarker panel, which is correct for discovery but heavily penalises a prespecified single hypothesis. The fix is therefore explicit: a first-line population, a time-to-event endpoint, no multiplicity penalty from unrelated biomarkers, and adjustment for PD-L1 and smoking. I expect a small, real, and prognostic-looking effect rather than the large predictive one the early literature claims.

prior_negative_evidence.summary: The null being re-tested. 439 patients enrolled, 305 sequenced, 58 STK11-mutant; STK11 OR 1.17 (0.634-2.17), AUC 0.54, p-adjusted 0.896, and no PFS association. Preprint, not peer reviewed. If a larger first-line time-to-event analysis also returns null, the STK11 resistance claim is in serious trouble and this hypothesis should die loudly rather than quietly.

In first-line immunotherapy, STK11 gave OS HR 1.4 (0.9-2.3, p=0.1) — nonsignificant, and identical in point estimate to the HR 1.4 (1.2-1.6) seen in the first-line chemotherapy arm of the same cohort. A second, larger, first-line null on the ICI side that also points to prognosis rather than prediction.
