plausibility.causal_story: None is offered. The stated chain runs: PIONeeR dichotomised its endpoint and adjusted p-values across many biomarkers, therefore it had low sensitivity; therefore a time-to-event first-line analysis will detect a modest effect. Those are claims about estimator behaviour, not about biology. The implied biological content — LKB1 loss shortens time to progression — is the association itself, and the mechanisms that would explain it (C-029, C-031) are neither invoked nor used to generate any prediction that separates this hypothesis from the prognostic account or from H-001.
mechanism_steps: Dichotomising a time-to-event outcome into a binary resistance label discards information and lowers power. (Statistical, not biological.)
Second-line populations are survivorship-selected, attenuating prognostic effects. (Selection, not mechanism — and the content of H-006.)
Multiplicity adjustment across an unrelated biomarker panel penalises a prespecified single hypothesis. (Analytic choice.)
Therefore a first-line time-to-event analysis will show a modest STK11 association. (Restatement of the correlation; no biological step is required for this to be true or false.)
alternative_explanations: The association is entirely prognostic — the same point estimate appears on first-line chemotherapy with no ICI present (C-037, HR 1.4) — so a positive result here would be uninformative about checkpoint blockade.
Residual confounding by PD-L1, smoking and performance status produces a modest hazard ratio of the size predicted without any LKB1-specific effect.
Selection into sequencing: patients sequenced before or early in first-line therapy differ systematically from those sequenced later, and STK11 prevalence tracks tissue adequacy and panel breadth.
confounding_risks: Prognostic vs predictive is unresolvable by construction: no non-ICI arm, so a within-ICI hazard ratio is exactly the estimand the field already has and cannot interpret.

Surveillance bias on a progression endpoint: real-world imaging intervals are irregular and clinicians who know a patient carries a resistance-associated genotype scan sooner, which inflates measured progression rates in the exposed group independently of biology.
Interval censoring: progression dates are ascertained at scan dates, so short-horizon differences are quantised by scheduling patterns that differ across sites and eras.
Immortal time via sequencing-conditioned entry, which is acute for a first-line PFS endpoint because sequencing frequently reports after treatment start.
Smoking and PD-L1 as the leading measured confounders, both incompletely captured.
Panel ascertainment: STK11 callability varies by assay, so the comparator group is contaminated with untested patients.
plausibility.reject_reason: There is no causal story here, only a measurement argument. Every reason given for expecting the association — dichotomisation of a time-to-event outcome, a second-line population, multiplicity adjustment across an unrelated biomarker panel — concerns how PIONeeR was analysed, not what LKB1 does. The statement itself, 'STK11 loss-of-function is associated with a modestly shorter time to progression or death on anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy', restates the correlation the field has already pooled across 14 studies and 4,317 patients (C-039, PFS HR 1.45). No step is proposed that could be false about biology, and no differential prediction is made: the candidate's own expectation is 'a small, real, and prognostic-looking effect', which by construction cannot distinguish prediction from prognosis in a design with no non-ICI comparator. H-001 asks the same underlying question with the comparator arm that makes it answerable; H-012 is that design with the discriminating contrast deleted, so it tests nothing H-001 does not test better. A methodological improvement on a prior null is a good reason to re-analyse someone else's data; it is not a hypothesis.

hypotheses.statement: In resectable NSCLC treated with neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy, KRAS/STK11 co-mutation is associated with shorter recurrence-free survival after resection without a correspondingly lower major pathologic response rate, i.e. pathologic response and durable disease control dissociate in this genotype.

origin.rationale: The graph contains a within-study dissociation nobody has the power to interpret: in the same tiny neoadjuvant cohort, KRAS/STK11 co-mutants had an RFS hazard ratio of 7.09 (p=0.027, n=52) while major pathologic response was 17% versus 25% (p=1.0, n=21, seven co-mutants). The MPR null is the buried negative — a nonsignificant result in a 21-patient comparison that would be read as reassurance. The reason to believe the dissociation is real rather than noise is mechanistic and testable: major pathologic response after neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy is driven substantially by the cytotoxic component, which LKB1 loss does not impair, whereas durable freedom from recurrence depends on immune control of residual microscopic disease, which requires the antigen presentation (C-031) and functional CD8 response (C-036 reports CD8 dysfunction rather than absence in STK11-deficient tumours) that LKB1 loss degrades. If that is right, MPR is a poor surrogate endpoint specifically in this genotype — which matters because MPR is increasingly used as the trial-level surrogate in the perioperative setting. Only a cohort linking genomics to surgical pathology and long-term recurrence at scale can test it.

prior_negative_evidence.identifier: PMID 39545922 (Rosner et al., Clin Cancer Res 2025;31:339-51)
prior_negative_evidence.summary: The primary report behind C-044/C-045 already describes significantly shorter RFS in KRAS-mutant/STK11-mutant tumours despite comparable pathologic response rates, with supporting bulk RNA sequencing on the tumour immune microenvironment. The dissociation is therefore published, not undiscovered, and novelty here is limited to replication with adequate power — the primary cohort had roughly seven co-mutant patients. Recorded because it substantially discounts this candidate.

Reports that KRAS and STK11 mutations shape the CD8+ T-cell response in resectable NSCLC after neoadjuvant therapy, supplying the immunologic correlate but again in a small surgical series with no independent RFS validation.

plausibility.causal_story: As proposed: platinum drives bulk tumour regression and hence major pathologic response, a process LKB1 loss does not impair, while freedom from recurrence depends on immune control of residual microscopic disease requiring antigen presentation (C-031) and functional CD8 responses (C-036) that LKB1 loss degrades; hence a dissociation, and hence MPR is a poor surrogate in this genotype. The first step fails: in neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy the pathologic response is largely the immunotherapy's contribution, so the same defect that impairs durable control should also impair pathologic response. With that step removed the mechanism predicts concordance, and the observed 'dissociation' reduces to a nonsignificant comparison in 21 patients read as evidence.
mechanism_steps: Neoadjuvant platinum doublet causes bulk cytoreduction independent of LKB1 status. (True in isolation.)

Major pathologic response therefore mainly measures the cytotoxic effect. (FALSE for chemo-immunotherapy: the pathologic response gain over chemotherapy alone is attributable to the checkpoint inhibitor.)
Durable freedom from recurrence requires immune surveillance of residual microscopic disease via MHC-I presentation and functional CD8 memory (C-031, C-036).
LKB1 loss degrades that surveillance, shortening recurrence-free survival.
Therefore recurrence-free survival is reduced while pathologic response is preserved. (Does not follow once step 2 is corrected; the corrected chain predicts both are reduced.)
alternative_explanations: The MPR null is sampling noise: 17% vs 25% with p=1.0 in 21 patients has an interval spanning almost the entire plausible range, so 'no difference' is uninformative rather than a buried negative.
The RFS signal is small-cell instability: HR 7.09 from roughly seven co-mutant patients is the kind of estimate that regresses hard toward the null on replication.

Stage and adjuvant-therapy imbalance: co-mutant patients may present with higher pathologic stage and receive different adjuvant treatment, which drives recurrence-free survival without any surrogate-endpoint dissociation.
confounding_risks: Surveillance intensity determines recurrence detection, and imaging frequency after resection varies by site, stage and clinician concern — a direct route to differential ascertainment of the RFS endpoint.
Selection into resection: patients who progress during neoadjuvant therapy never reach surgery, which removes the worst-outcome exposed patients and distorts both endpoints in opposite directions.
Pathologic response assessment is not standardised across institutions, and residual-viable-tumour scoring is observer-dependent.
Adjuvant therapy receipt after resection is a post-baseline variable on the causal path to recurrence.
Immortal time between diagnosis, sequencing and resection.

Prognostic vs predictive: no non-immunotherapy neoadjuvant comparator exists in current practice, so the surrogate-failure claim cannot be attributed to the ICI component even if the dissociation were observed.
plausibility.reject_reason: The dissociation requires that major pathologic response after neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy is driven by the cytotoxic component and is therefore LKB1-independent. That premise is false: pathologic response in this setting is overwhelmingly attributable to the checkpoint inhibitor added to chemotherapy — pathologic complete response rises roughly tenfold when anti-PD-1 is added to neoadjuvant platinum doublet, against a low single-digit rate for chemotherapy alone. So the very antigen-presentation and priming defects the hypothesis invokes to explain the recurrence-free survival deficit (C-031, C-029, C-036) predict a LOWER major pathologic response rate as well. Followed honestly, the mechanism predicts concordance between the two endpoints, not the claimed dissociation. The other limb is worse: 'no correspondingly lower MPR' rests on 17% versus 25% with p=1.0 in 21 patients, of whom 7 were co-mutant (C-045). Sampling noise is a complete explanation for that null and no biology is needed. The RFS limb (C-044, HR 7.09) comes from a review restating a primary report the mapper never opened, in a cohort of the same 7 co-mutants. Building a surrogate-endpoint claim on a seven-patient cell whose non-significant arm is treated as a finding inverts the evidence.

hypotheses.statement: Biallelic STK11 inactivation is associated with shorter overall survival on ICI-containing therapy than monoallelic or missense-only STK11 alteration, and monoallelic missense STK11 alteration behaves like STK11 wild-type.

origin.rationale: This is the established-mechanism-whose-clinical-implication-was-never-tested case, and it may be the single best explanation for why the graph disagrees with itself. LKB1 is a classic two-hit tumour suppressor, and every mechanism in the graph — STING silencing via SAM/DNMT1/EZH2 (C-029, C-030) and loss of immunoproteasome-dependent presentation (C-031) — requires the kinase activity to be gone, not merely reduced. Li et al. make the same argument from the other direction, showing the transcriptomic STK11-deficient phenotype rather than mutation status identifies ICB-refractory tumours (C-034), with the companion claim that tissue mutation alone does not (C-035, unverified and so discounted here). Every clinical cohort in the graph defines exposure as 'STK11 mutated', pooling true biallelic loss with heterozygous missense variants of uncertain effect. That non-differential-looking but actually directional misclassification would attenuate estimates toward the null and would do so by different amounts in cohorts with different panel content and different variant-calling thresholds — which is exactly the pattern of disagreement seen between Skoulidis, Papillon-Cavanagh, the Japanese C-CAT cohort and PIONeeR, and it also fits the unexplained prevalence spread from 8.6% to 25% (C-048). A cohort with copy-number and zygosity calls alongside mutation calls can separate the strata; no published cohort in this graph has.

prior_negative_evidence.identifier: J Thorac Oncol S1556-0864(24)00081-9, 'Precision Immunotherapy for STK11/KEAP1-Mutant NSCLC'
prior_negative_evidence.summary: Review that already argues clonality, allelic status and variant class should stratify treatment: it states that clonal mutations with LOH in KEAP1, unlike subclonal ones, associate with resistance and a T-cell-excluded microenvironment, and recommends that subclonal or benign-predicted missense variants with high PD-L1 should not be steered away from PD-(L)1 monotherapy. The idea is therefore in print for KEAP1; the STK11-specific effect estimate is what is missing, which is what the mapper independently found in coverage note 6.

prior_negative_evidence.identifier: J Thorac Oncol S1556-0864(25)00049-8, 'Gene Copy Deletion of STK11, KEAP1, and SMARCA4: Clinicopathologic Features and Association With the Outcomes of Immunotherapy With or Without Chemotherapy in Nonsquamous NSCLC'
prior_negative_evidence.summary: A 2025 study that specifically addresses copy deletion of STK11 and immunotherapy outcomes — the closest existing work to this hypothesis. The full text returned HTTP 403 to automated retrieval so its effect estimates and whether it separated biallelic from monoallelic events could not be confirmed; it must be read before this candidate is pre-registered, and it may substantially reduce or eliminate the gap.

Argues from transcriptomic phenotype that mutation status is a poor proxy for functional STK11 loss, and reports the phenotype rather than the mutation identifies ICB-refractory tumours. Supports the premise but also means the 'mutation is a poor proxy' claim is established; the novelty is in using zygosity as a genomic proxy for the functional state, which a clinicogenomic dataset can compute and a transcriptomic signature cannot.

exposure.genomic_criteria: STK11 homozygous deletion, or a truncating variant (nonsense, frameshift, splice-site) together with loss of heterozygosity or a second qualifying variant at the STK11 locus; where available, high variant allele fraction adjusted for tumour purity is used as the supporting zygosity signal
exposure.treatment_criteria: first-line ICI-containing therapy, regimen class entered as a covariate

comparator.description: Two explicit comparator strata rather than one: (a) monoallelic STK11 alteration, defined as a single truncating or oncogenic missense variant with retained heterozygosity, and (b) STK11 wild-type. The hypothesis predicts stratum (a) resembles stratum (b) and both differ from the exposed group.

inclusion: copy-number or LOH information available at STK11
tumour purity estimate available or variant allele fraction reported

panels that do not report copy number

proposed_covariates: tumour purity and sequencing panel identity, since zygosity inference degrades with low purity and differs across assays
specimen type (primary versus metastatic, archival versus fresh)

plausibility.causal_story: LKB1 is a classical two-hit tumour suppressor, and every downstream mechanism in the graph requires kinase activity to be abolished rather than halved: AMPK signalling is dose-sensitive, and the SAM/DNMT1/EZH2 route to STING silencing (C-029/C-030) and the immunoproteasome/autophagy route to defective presentation (C-031) are both consequences of losing the kinase, not of losing one allele. A tumour with a single heterozygous missense variant retains substantial LKB1 activity and should behave like wild-type; a tumour with homozygous deletion, or a truncating variant plus LOH, has none and should carry the full phenotype. Because published cohorts all define exposure as 'STK11 mutated' and therefore pool the two, their estimates are attenuated by an amount that depends on panel content, variant-calling thresholds and purity — which predicts both the direction of the zygosity gradient and the pattern of cross-cohort disagreement, including the unexplained prevalence spread from 8.6% to 25% (C-048). The falsifiable step is dose-sensitivity: if haploinsufficiency is enough to silence STING, monoallelic cases will not resemble wild-type. C-035 is unverified and is not used as support here.
mechanism_steps: LKB1 acts as a two-hit tumour suppressor; complete loss requires inactivation of both alleles, commonly truncating variant plus LOH or homozygous deletion.
AMPK activation, and hence restraint on mTORC1 and one-carbon flux, is dose-dependent on residual LKB1 kinase activity.
The SAM surplus needed to hyperactivate DNMT1/EZH2 and silence STING (C-029/C-030) arises only when that restraint is effectively absent.
The immunoproteasome and autophagy phenotype (C-031) likewise reflects loss of kinase function rather than allelic dosage alone.
Therefore biallelic cases carry the full immune-evasion phenotype while monoallelic missense cases substantially retain it, behaving like wild-type.
Pooling the two attenuates published estimates by an assay-dependent amount, which predicts the observed heterogeneity between cohorts as well as the gradient itself.
alternative_explanations: Zygosity is a proxy for tumour purity and specimen quality: high-purity, high-tumour-content samples are more often called biallelic, and purity correlates with disease burden and biopsy site, which independently predict survival.

Clonality rather than zygosity is the operative variable — a clonal heterozygous truncating event may matter more than a subclonal biallelic one — so a positive gradient does not establish that allelic dose is the mechanism.
Selection effects: panels reporting copy number are newer and concentrated at particular institutions and eras, so the biallelic-callable subcohort differs systematically from the rest.
confounding_risks: Measurement is the central threat: LOH and copy-number inference from targeted panels degrades with low tumour purity, and misclassification is directional — low-purity samples are called monoallelic — so the exposure contrast is partly a purity contrast that also predicts outcome.
Panel ascertainment: only some assays report copy number at STK11, so the analysable population is non-random with respect to institution, era and disease burden.
Specimen type: metastatic and archival specimens differ in purity and in the reliability of allelic-imbalance calls compared with primary resections.

Prognostic vs predictive: no non-ICI arm, so a real zygosity gradient could be entirely prognostic — biallelic loss marking more aggressive disease — which is the more parsimonious reading given C-037.
KEAP1 zygosity is correlated and, per the cited review, is the version of this idea already in print; without joint modelling the STK11 gradient may be a KEAP1 gradient.
Immortal time via sequencing-conditioned entry, aggravated because zygosity-callable sequencing is often later-generation and therefore later in the disease course.

hypotheses.statement: In advanced NSCLC treated with anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy, the excess hazard associated with STK11 loss-of-function is concentrated in the early months after treatment start and diminishes thereafter, i.e. the STK11 effect is front-loaded and the proportional-hazards assumption fails for it.

origin.rationale: Every claim in the graph reports a single hazard ratio or a single response proportion, and no claim examines the shape of the effect over time. Yet the shape is what would reconcile the literature. Response-based and short-horizon metrics show large STK11 effects (pooled ORR 10.1% versus 25.8%, C-040; pooled PFS HR 1.45, C-039), while randomized long-horizon survival comparisons show little or none (KEYNOTE-042 C-018, POSEIDON C-042) and a second-line prospective cohort finds no primary-resistance signal (C-046). A front-loaded hazard produces exactly that pattern: it inflates response and early-progression metrics, is partially averaged away in an overall survival hazard ratio, and is attenuated in populations already filtered by survivorship. The mechanism predicts the shape rather than merely accommodating it. Silenced STING (C-029), a compromised immunoproteasome (C-031) and a myeloid-suppressed microenvironment (C-027) are all failures of the initial priming step; a tumour whose priming fails does so within the first cycles, whereas patients whose tumours do prime are not disadvantaged thereafter. The clinical implication has never been stated or tested: STK11 should identify patients who need an early response assessment, not patients who should be denied checkpoint blockade.

prior_negative_evidence.summary: Pooled 14 retrospective studies (4317 patients) into single PFS and OS hazard ratios with no assessment of time-varying effects or non-proportional hazards. Because the pooled estimates assume proportionality, they cannot detect the pattern this hypothesis proposes, and their existence is not evidence against it — but it does mean a great deal of data has been analysed without anyone asking the question.

Used a binary primary-resistance label, which is the crudest possible summary of an early-hazard phenomenon, and found nothing. If the effect were strongly front-loaded, a primary-resistance endpoint should have been the most sensitive design available and it was null — this is the strongest evidence against the hypothesis and is recorded as such.

Randomized phase IIb of durvalumab plus tremelimumab plus chemotherapy versus pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy restricted to STK11/KEAP1/KRAS-mutated non-squamous NSCLC, 103 patients, active and not recruiting, no results posted. Its primary endpoint is PFS with 6- and 12-month PFS rates, so it will eventually speak to early-versus-late separation in this genotype; the hypothesis should be tested before that reads out or reframed once it does.

exposure.description: STK11 loss-of-function, with the effect estimated as a function of time since treatment start rather than as a single constant hazard ratio
exposure.genomic_criteria: STK11 nonsense, frameshift, splice-site, homozygous deletion, or oncogenic/likely-oncogenic missense
exposure.treatment_criteria: first-line anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy, monotherapy or chemo-immunotherapy, regimen class entered as a covariate

comparator.description: STK11 wild-type patients on the same first-line ICI-containing regimen class; the estimand is the contrast between the STK11 hazard ratio in an early prespecified interval after treatment start and the hazard ratio in the subsequent interval, among patients still at risk at the interval boundary.

population.description: Adults with advanced NSCLC on first-line ICI-containing therapy with panel sequencing covering STK11 and sufficient follow-up to observe both intervals
inclusion: first-line ICI-containing therapy
follow-up extending past the prespecified interval boundary for patients not experiencing an event
exclusion: patients whose only follow-up is the sequencing encounter

hypotheses.proposed_endpoint_concept: overall survival from start of first-line ICI-containing therapy, with the hazard contrast estimated separately in an early and a later prespecified interval
proposed_covariates: ECOG performance status, which itself drives early events and must not be allowed to masquerade as a front-loaded genomic effect
disease burden and presence of liver or brain metastases at baseline where recorded
left truncation at sequencing report date, which is critical here because early deaths are systematically missing from cohorts that require a sequencing result to enter

plausibility.causal_story: As proposed: STING silencing (C-029), immunoproteasome failure (C-031) and myeloid suppression (C-027) are all failures of initial priming, so tumours that will not respond declare themselves within the first cycles while tumours that do prime carry no later disadvantage; hence a front-loaded excess hazard and non-proportional hazards. The biology is not implausible, but the predicted observable — a declining hazard ratio — is produced just as readily by frailty selection in a heterogeneous population with a constant individual-level effect, and by the differential left truncation this cohort design imposes. Because the hypothesis offers no observable that separates the mechanistic account from those two, a positive result would not be evidence for the mechanism.
mechanism_steps: LKB1 loss disables innate licensing (STING, C-029), MHC-I peptide supply (C-031) and adds myeloid suppression (C-027, mouse, contested by C-009).
Those are all failures of the initial priming step rather than of response maintenance.
Tumours that cannot prime progress within the first treatment cycles.
Patients whose tumours do prime are not disadvantaged thereafter, so the excess hazard decays.
Therefore the STK11 hazard ratio is larger in an early interval than in a later one. (True also under frailty selection with a constant effect, so the observation does not identify the mechanism.)
alternative_explanations: Frailty/depletion of susceptibles: a constant individual-level hazard ratio in a heterogeneous population yields a declining marginal hazard ratio automatically, which fully reproduces the predicted pattern with no LKB1-specific biology.

Baseline severity: STK11-mutant patients have higher disease burden and worse performance status at treatment start, so early deaths cluster in the exposed group for reasons that are prognostic and not immune-mechanistic.

Left truncation: requiring a sequencing result to enter removes early deaths differentially, which distorts the early-interval hazard ratio in a direction that depends on turnaround time rather than biology.
confounding_risks: Immortal time and left truncation dominate: the early window is precisely the window that sequencing-conditioned entry under-samples, and truncation intervals differ by institution, panel and disease burden.
ECOG and baseline tumour burden (liver and brain metastases) drive early events and are recorded coarsely; they can masquerade as a front-loaded genomic effect.
Treatment discontinuation and hospice transition patterns in the first months differ by genotype-associated disease severity and are rarely captured.
Prognostic vs predictive: no non-ICI comparator, so a front-loaded hazard cannot be attributed to failed priming under checkpoint blockade rather than to aggressive disease.
Interval boundary selection is a researcher degree of freedom; the estimate depends on where the boundary is placed and must be prespecified, but even prespecified it is not identifying.
Panel ascertainment and era, as elsewhere, both of which correlate with sequencing turnaround and hence with the truncation problem above.
plausibility.reject_reason: A hazard ratio that declines with time is the generic signature of unmeasured heterogeneity, not evidence of a priming-failure mechanism. In any population with a frailty distribution, the frail exposed patients leave the risk set first and the marginal hazard ratio drifts toward one even when the individual-level ratio is exactly constant. The proposed mechanism therefore predicts a pattern that its leading alternative predicts equally well, and no discriminator is offered: the design cannot distinguish 'LKB1-deficient tumours fail priming within the first cycles' from 'STK11 marks aggressive disease and the most aggressive die first'. The hypothesis is also the one most damaged by its own acknowledged design flaw — the early interval carries the entire signal, and the early interval is exactly what a sequencing-conditioned cohort under-observes, because patients must survive to be sequenced. Left truncation removes the very events the hypothesis is about, and no amount of adjustment recovers them. Finally, nothing in the chain is ICI-specific: early excess death in an aggressive genotype is expected on chemotherapy too, and with no non-ICI arm the 'needs early response assessment, not denial of checkpoint blockade' implication does not follow from a positive result. The strongest on-point evidence, PIONeeR's binary primary-resistance endpoint, is the design most sensitive to a front-loaded effect and it was null (C-046).

Rejects: H-003 (exposure is a proxy for smoking and co-mutation background already in the model; no ancestry-to-LKB1 step), H-005 (mechanism rests on a mouse claim C-027 that failed replication in C-009, and the compounding step does not fix a direction), H-006 (platinum-compensation limb is self-defeating because STING silencing removes the sensor for the ligand platinum supplies; the remaining limb is survivorship selection, and first- vs second-line monotherapy strata differ structurally on PD-L1), H-012 (no causal story, only an endpoint and multiplicity argument; restates the pooled correlation and deletes the comparator contrast that makes H-001 answerable), H-013 (pathologic response after neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy is largely ICI-driven, so the mechanism predicts concordance rather than the claimed dissociation; the MPR null is noise from 21 patients), H-015 (a declining hazard ratio is the generic signature of frailty selection and of left truncation, so the prediction does not discriminate the proposed mechanism from its alternatives).

CROSS-CUTTING NOTE ON PROGNOSTIC VS PREDICTIVE. This is the dominant confounding axis across the whole set and it is recorded in confounding_risks for every hypothesis. Only H-001 and H-010 carry a treatment contrast capable of addressing it, and H-010's contrast is between two ICI-containing regimens rather than against a non-ICI arm. The published designs with non-ICI comparators point toward prognosis (Papillon-Cavanagh interaction HR 1.05 for PFS and 1.13 for OS, C-012/C-013; Shire HR 1.4 on first-line chemotherapy with no ICI, C-037, against HR 1.4 nonsignificant on first-line ICI, C-038; KEYNOTE-042 OS HR 0.37 in STK11-mutants versus 0.83 in wild-type, C-018). The pooled PFS HR of 1.45 (C-039) is a within-ICI-arm estimate from single-arm retrospective cohorts and is not an interaction test; it should not be read as evidence of prediction anywhere downstream. Any hypothesis in this file that returns a positive within-ICI-arm result should be interpreted as prognostic until a non-ICI comparator says otherwise.

C-035 is unverified (no supporting quote, publisher 403) and was discounted. It appears only in H-014's supporting claims, where stage 2 already used it as corroboration rather than support; the plausibility assessment for H-014 rests on C-034, C-029/C-030, C-031 and established two-hit tumour-suppressor biology, and states the discounting explicitly.

THREE PASSES CARRY MEDIATOR-CONDITIONING HAZARDS that stage 4 should note in the analysis plan rather than treat as ordinary covariates: H-007 and H-008 stratify on PD-L1, which is downstream of the exposure via the interferon axis, so both estimate controlled direct effects and are open to collider bias; H-004 lists TMB as a covariate while C-032 places TMB on the causal path. These are stated in each hypothesis's confounding_risks and are not grounds for rejection, but the estimand must be labelled.

H-007 and H-008 make partially opposing predictions in the overlapping PD-L1-high stratum (H-007 predicts the KL-vs-KP ordering survives PD-L1 stratification; H-008 predicts the STK11 penalty vanishes at TPS >= 50%). They differ in genotype contrast, endpoint and line, so both survive stage 3, but they should be pre-registered as a pair and interpreted jointly rather than separately.
